text:
incidents-bot: Detected repeated OOMs in serving-runtime (paged-attn allocator) on gpu-pool-usw2-node-7, node flap count=3 in 10m, auto-evict triggered but mem pressure persists. Error: CUDA OOM during allocation of kv-cache slab.
Jordan (oncall): seeing the bot alerts, confirmed node 7 and node 9 flapped, container restarted automatically twice. I'm cordoning node-7 to stop new pods.
Alex W: logs from node-7 attached below. Noticed slow memory creep from paged-kv allocator, fragmentation spikes before OOM.
Alex W: ```
[2026-03-15T01:12:03Z] serving: alloc slab_request size=432MB -> failed: CUDA_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T01:12:03Z] pager: free_pages=12 total_pages=4096 frag_ratio=0.87
[2026-03-15T01:12:03Z] kvcache: eviction_attempts=4 reclaimed=5MB
[2026-03-15T01:12:04Z] runtime: container restart, exit_code=137
```
Maria T: can you dump the kvcache bitmap / occupancy? frag_ratio 0.87 is high.
Alex W: running a lightweight dump now, output: occupancy pattern shows many small live segments separated by low-util gaps -> classic micro-fragmentation with paged allocator.
Prashant R: any correlation with recent model rollout or sequence length changes?
Jordan (oncall): traffic skew to long-seq customers around 00:30 UTC, matches spike in seq length p95 from 128->512 for certain routes.
Alex W: yes, long sequences make the pager allocate many pages then free unevenly. Also we saw a background warmup job that preloads KV for a recently onboarded model. That likely contributed.
Jordan (oncall): customer impact: ~3% requests in us-west-2 seeing 500 errors during flaps, critical customers A and C report degraded responses. QPS on the affected pool dropped 20% with latency spikes.
Maria T: mitigation proposal (short term): 1) reduce per-request max_seq_length to 256 for the pool (enforce via route policy), 2) bump kvcache eviction aggressiveness to reclaim earlier, 3) disable attention paging for the largest model until we fix fragmentation heuristics.
Prashant R: agree. Also recommend immediate rolling-restart with env REDWOOD_KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.5 and REDWOOD_PAGER_DEFRAg=true (defrag hint) for the node pool.
Jordan (oncall): I'm going to apply a node taint for new pods and drain node-7 and node-9 gracefully, then restart the runtime pods with the evict threshold change. Applying now: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-pool-usw2-node-7 node.flapping=true:NoSchedule`
runtime-alerts-bot: Notified eng-runtime paging-oncall. Pager metric spike > 4sigma, alert id: PAGED-ALLOC-1172.
Alex W: before restart, snapshotting /var/log/runtime/kv_stats and creating a core dump for one crashed container at /var/crash/serving-2101234567-core.gz. Uploaded to s3://redwood-dumps/2101234567-core.gz
Jordan (oncall): rolling restart started. Commands I ran: `kubectl set env deployment/serving REDWOOD_KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.5 REDWOOD_DISABLE_PAGED_ATTENTION=true --namespace=prod-usw2` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/serving --namespace=prod-usw2`
Maria T: after restart, keep traffic low. I'm configuring route policy to redirect 40% of traffic to eu-central for affected routes to reduce pressure.
Prashant R: please also patch the kubelet OOM score adjustments for the runtime container (reduce oom_score_adj) to make host reclaim more likely for non-runtime processes.
Jordan (oncall): monitored post-restart: memory usage dropped ~20% on nodes, frag ratio dropped to 0.62 on node-8 and 0.65 on node-12, node-7 remains ~0.7 but stable for now. No additional container restarts in 9m.
Alex W: observed one CUDA error during restart sequence: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in cublas kernel, probably side-effect of abrupt restart and mixed GPU driver state. Nvidia driver logs show GPU reset between restarts. We're re-creating pods one-by-one to avoid driver reset storms.
Maria T: customer impact update: critical customers rate of 500s reduced to 0.5%, overall error budget back within SLA for now. Notifying support to update status page.
Jordan (oncall): next actions: 1) keep route diversion for 60m, 2) schedule eng-runtime hotfix to improve defragmentation heuristics and smarter eviction (owner: Prashant), 3) postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps (owner: Alex).
Prashant R: will open a PR with improved eviction policy and a background compaction pass for paged allocator. I will also add better telemetry: kvcache hole sizes, compaction time, and per-request page churn.
Alex W: will attach the logs and heap snapshots to the incident ticket and create a follow-up task to test the hotspot: simulate long-seq workload with synthetic traffic to reproduce fragmentation.
runtime-alerts-bot: Auto-attach runbook 'paged-alloc-frag' and create incident ticket INC-2101.
Jordan (oncall): marking this thread handoff to eng-runtime. If any of you see new flaps re-open pager and tag me.
Maria T: quick note — avoid full cluster restarts; we should prefer pod-by-pod restarts to minimize GPU driver resets. Learned that the hard way here.
Alex W: thanks all. I'll draft the postmortem, include the customer impact numbers and mitigation timeline.
Jordan (oncall): closing handoff at 01:42 UTC, please update INC-2101 with any additional findings. :thumbsup:
